# Strategic Relationship Assessment

A 10-question relationship assessment in Thai. Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL through `pg` with plain SQL. All user-facing text is Thai.

## Commands

```bash
npm run db:dev      # local PostgreSQL on port 5432, no install needed; keep running
npm run db:migrate  # apply db/schema.sql; safe to repeat
npm run dev         # http://localhost:3000
npm run typecheck
npm run build
```

Setup: copy `.env.example` to `.env`, then set `ADMIN_PASSWORD`. There is no automated test suite, so check changes by clicking through the app in a browser.

## Working with the owner

After every change, start the local database and app, open the changed page, and leave them running so the owner can review it. Only offer to commit or push after that. Never run the review against the production database.

## Where things are

- `lib/quiz.ts`: scoring and all result wording (the questions are no longer here, see the next two entries)
- `lib/builtInQuestions.ts`: the built-in questions and the category titles. It has no imports on purpose, because `scripts/migrate.mjs` compiles it alone to seed version 1. It is also the fallback when the database cannot be read
- `lib/questionSet.ts`, `app/backoffice/settings/questions/`, `components/QuestionsForm.tsx`: **versioned questions and answers.** Every save in Settings > คำถามและคำตอบ inserts a new row in `question_sets` (`version` 1, 2, 3 under an advisory lock, `created_at`, optional `note`, `content` jsonb); rows are immutable (a trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE), so old sets stay for tracking, and saving identical content creates nothing. The highest valid version is what visitors see: `/quiz` stays static and reads it through `getPublicQuestionSet()` (cached with the settings tag, texts only, **never the scores**). The 10 questions, their order and which category each belongs to are fixed; an administrator edits the wording and the score of each of the 3 answers, and the **category text**: for each of the 3 categories a heading shown above its questions and a short name shown on the result page (`content.categories`, part of every version; a row saved before this existed has none and reads as the built-in text). The explanation and advice text per category and status on the result page (`categoryCopy` in `lib/quiz.ts`) is still in code. **Score rule: the three answers of every question score exactly 0, 1 and 2, one each, no repeats** (`validateQuestionSet`, shared by the form, the action and the readers, with Thai messages). A question is therefore worth 2, the maximums stay 6, 6, 8 and 20, and the safety rule became: any answer scoring 0 in a category 1 question sets `safetyFlag`. `responses.question_set_version` (required, default 1, foreign key) stores the version a visitor was shown; the quiz posts `{answers, version}`, the API scores against that version's set (a missing version means 1, for pages built before versions existed), and the results page scores with the response's own version, so an edit never changes an old result. Statistics (`/backoffice/report`, `/backoffice/charts`) are about one version (`?version=N`, newest by default) because a position means a different answer in another version; colours follow the answer's score, not its position. The edit form has **three tabs, one per category** (`components/QuestionsForm.tsx`): all three are one form, so switching tabs loses nothing and one Save creates one version with every change from every tab; a mistake on a hidden tab switches to the first tab with a mistake and shows a count badge on it, each tab shows how many items were edited, the tab is kept in the address (`?tab=2`), and leaving with unsaved edits asks first. A save goes through the same flow as the other settings (password or code, email, `ScrollToTop`, front-end validation), with the `questions` type in `lib/pending.ts` and `applyChange`
- `lib/courses.ts`: the built-in course data (defaults). Administrators can override each course in the backoffice; each course is one `settings` row named `course:<key>` holding the form values as JSON. `scripts/migrate.mjs` inserts a row for every built-in course that has none (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a deploy never overwrites an edit), and "reset" writes the built-in text back into the row. If a row is missing or invalid the page still falls back to the built-in text. Changing `lib/courses.ts` therefore only affects courses that have no row yet
- `lib/courseEdit.ts`: editable course fields, limits and validation, shared by the edit form, the server action and the settings reader. `app/backoffice/settings/courses/` and `components/CourseForm.tsx` are the edit pages
- `lib/lineLink.ts`: the default LINE link, its validation (https and line.me or lin.ee only) and the account name derived from it (`LINE: @aj.kwan`, or `LINE Official` for short links)
- `lib/settings.ts`: reads the `settings` table (key and value, one row per setting; no row means the built-in default). `getSettings()` is cached and never throws; `readSettingsNow()` is uncached for the settings page
- `app/backoffice/settings/`: the Settings tab has a sub menu (`components/SettingsNav.tsx`, rendered by `app/backoffice/settings/layout.tsx`, so the code page and the course edit pages show it too): **ติดต่อ** at `/backoffice/settings` (the LINE link; saving clears the `settings` cache tag and `revalidatePath('/', 'layout')`), **รายละเอียดคอร์ส** at `/backoffice/settings/courses` (the course list; each course edits at `/backoffice/settings/courses/<key>` and keeps this item highlighted) and **คำถามและคำตอบ** at `/backoffice/settings/questions` (the versioned question editor, with a version history and a read-only page per version at `/backoffice/settings/questions/versions/<n>`). `components/TwoFactorStatus.tsx` is the 2FA status block shown on the contact and course list pages. A new settings page goes into `SettingsNav` and uses the same layout
- `lib/adminAuth.ts`: the admin login check, used by the middleware and again inside server actions
- `lib/confirmPassword.ts`: constant-time check of the administrator password typed on the settings form, which every settings change must include while `TWO_FACTOR_AUTHEN` is off. `lib/passwordLock.ts` holds the limits read from `PASSWORD_MAX_ATTEMPTS` and `PASSWORD_LOCK_MINUTES` (through `lib/envNumber.ts`, which falls back to the default for a missing or invalid value), `lib/changeFlow.ts` does the counting and locking, `lib/lockMessages.ts` and `components/LockNotice.tsx` show the tries left and the lock on the settings pages
- `lib/notify.ts`, `components/MailNotice.tsx`: after every successful settings or course change (save or reset) the administrator is emailed through Resend: Bangkok and UTC time, each changed setting with old and new value (cut at 200 characters), the requester's IP and browser (email only, never stored), a warning that an unexpected change may mean the site is attacked or hacked, and the steps to shut down (`MAINTENANCE_MODE`) and investigate. Sending runs after the save and never blocks or undoes it; the redirect carries `mail=sent|failed|off` and the settings pages show it. A wrong password sends nothing
- `lib/twoFactor.ts`, `lib/otp.ts`, `lib/pending.ts`, `lib/changeFlow.ts`, `lib/applyChange.ts`, `app/backoffice/settings/verify/`: two-factor authentication for settings changes, switched by the `TWO_FACTOR_AUTHEN` environment variable (`on`). Off: the typed password is checked and the change is applied. On: the forms have no password box; saving only creates a pending change in the `otp_challenges` table (JSON in `payload`) and emails a 6-digit code to `ADMIN_EMAIL`, and the change is applied only when the code is entered on the verify page. Codes are random, stored only as a keyed hash, valid 10 minutes, single use, and by default 5 tries per code and 3 requests per 15 minutes (`OTP_TTL_MINUTES`, `OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `OTP_MAX_REQUESTS`, `OTP_REQUEST_WINDOW_MINUTES`); a new request retires older ones. Every change goes through `applyChange` in `lib/applyChange.ts`, so both paths write and notify the same way
- `lib/securityLog.ts`: one structured JSON line per security event (`login_failed`, `login_locked`, `password_failed`, `password_locked`, `otp_requested`, `otp_rate_limited`, `otp_wrong`, `otp_cancelled`, `change_applied`, `quiz_rate_limited`) in the application log. Never put a password, code, address or name in it
- `lib/secureEqual.ts`: constant-time string comparison that also runs in the Edge runtime; `hasAdminAccess` uses it
- `lib/rateLimit.ts`: in-memory per-address counter for the quiz API (nothing stored, so the no-IP-storage rule holds); `app/api/responses/route.ts` also refuses a body over 2 KB (413) and, through `countRecentResponses`, more than `RESPONSES_PER_MINUTE` (default 120) saved quizzes a minute for the whole site; `QUIZ_IP_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 10) is the per-address limit
- `lib/db.ts`: connection pool and every SQL query. `createChallengeLimited` checks the code-request limit and inserts the code in one transaction under an advisory lock, so parallel requests cannot pass the limit
- `db/schema.sql`: the tables `responses`, `settings`, `otp_challenges`, `password_failures`, `login_failures` and `question_sets` (`migrate.mjs` seeds version 1, stamps older responses with version 1, then makes `responses.question_set_version` required)
- `components/LineQr.tsx`: a QR code for the current LINE link, drawn on the server as inline SVG with `qrcode-generator` (no script, no outside service, so the content security policy is unchanged; black on white with a 4-module quiet zone, error correction M). It is passed to `Courses` as the `qr` prop from the results page, so it sits in the consultation card and is hidden with the courses for a safety result. It follows the saved LINE link, so changing the link changes the code. Check changes by decoding a screenshot with an independent reader, not by eye
- `components/ScrollToTop.tsx`: a client component that jumps to the top of the page when it mounts. Put it next to every error message that follows a failed submit and next to the success message after a save (server pages give it `key={Date.now()}` so it fires again on each failed save; `Quiz` and `CourseForm` scroll from their own state), and show that message at the top of the page or form, so the scroll lands on it. A new form with an error message needs the same
- Front-end validation: the backoffice forms check the same rules as the server before anything is sent, using the shared pure functions (`validateCourse` in `components/CourseForm.tsx`, `validateLineUrl` in `components/LineUrlInput.tsx`), so a mistake shows at once with the same Thai message and no request is made. The server actions validate again, always: a browser check can be skipped. A new field's rule goes in `lib/courseEdit.ts` or `lib/lineLink.ts` so both sides get it
- `components/Quiz.tsx`, `components/Courses.tsx`: the client components with state; `components/BackofficeNav.tsx` is a client component only to highlight the current menu item
- `app/api/responses/route.ts`: saves a completed quiz
- `app/backoffice/`: the menu is สถิติรายข้อ, การใช้งาน and ตั้งค่า. สถิติรายข้อ has two views chosen by a sub menu (`components/QuestionStatsHeader.tsx`): numbers at `/backoffice/report` and pie charts at `/backoffice/charts`, and `BackofficeNav` keeps the tab highlighted on both. Both views take `?period=range&from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` (no `period`, or `period=all`, means all time), read by `parsePeriod` in `lib/dateRange.ts` with no length limit and applied by `getAnswerCounts(range)` in Bangkok days; `components/PeriodFilter.tsx` is the all time or date range choice, and the sub menu links carry the chosen period. The date range usage report (the usage page also draws a line chart of completed quizzes per day with `components/LineChart.tsx`, plain SVG with no library or script so the content security policy needs no change; quick 7/30/90/365 day links come from `lastDays` in `lib/dateRange.ts`); `lib/stats.ts` turns counts into percentages and `lib/dateRange.ts` validates dates. Usage counts completed quizzes per Bangkok day; there are no user identities, and quiz starts aren't recorded
- `middleware.ts`: refuses methods other than GET, HEAD, POST and OPTIONS (405), then Basic auth for `/admin` and `/backoffice` (username `admin`), and maintenance mode for everything else. The middleware cannot reach the database, so for a request that carries a login it calls `app/api/auth/check/route.ts` (Node), which counts the try in `login_failures` before comparing (`lib/loginThrottle.ts`: `LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` default 20, `LOGIN_LOCK_MINUTES` default 15; one count shared by everyone; a lock refuses even the right password, and the administrator is emailed once; a correct login clears the count) and answers 204, 401 or 429. If the check cannot run the middleware answers 503, never lets the request in. `/api/auth/check` stays reachable in maintenance mode because the middleware depends on it. The first request without a login only gets the browser prompt and is not counted. The middleware also refuses a cross-site POST to the backoffice (403) and a POST with a declared body over 256 KB (413). With `MAINTENANCE_MODE=on` every public path returns a Thai 503 page (`lib/maintenance.ts`, with the helplines from `lib/helplines.ts`) and `/api/*` returns a 503 JSON error, so nothing can be saved; the backoffice stays reachable. The matcher covers all paths except `_next/static`, `_next/image` and the favicon, so it also closes the prebuilt `/` and `/quiz`
- `docs/`: Word copies of the design specification and installation manual

## Rules

- **Safety override:** the most severe answer on any of questions 1-3 sets `safetyFlag`. The report must then be critical whatever the total, show helplines and hide all courses and consultation offers. Never weaken this; a high score must not read as "safe" to someone reporting violence.
- **Course wording:** the course copy in `lib/courses.ts` is the client's own marketing text, supplied by the owner and published as written, including strong claims (subconscious control, "100%", "เสพติดเซ็กส์", "คลานเข่ากลับมา"). Keep it as supplied (this applies to the defaults, and the administrator's own edits are stored and shown as typed): don't soften or reword it unprompted, and don't add new claims of your own. The owner was told of the consumer-protection risk of absolute claims such as "100%" and price promises such as "ไม่มีทางกลับมาอีก", and chose to keep them. Never turn the headings into instructions for getting around a block, contacting someone who asked for no contact, or pressuring anyone.
- **Privacy:** never store names, contact details or IP addresses with responses. Answers are sensitive, so keep report and admin pages `noindex` and all queries parameterised.
- **Scoring stays on the server.** A response stores the position of each chosen answer; the score of a position comes from the question set of the version stored with the response (in version 1 the order is red, yellow, green, so the index is the score). Reports and results recalculate from `answers` and that version, so an edit of the questions never changes an old response, but a change to the scoring or result wording in code still affects old reports. Never send scores to the browser.
- Add schema changes to `db/schema.sql` in a form that is safe to run repeatedly.
- **Settings:** public pages must read settings with the cached `getSettings()`, never from the database directly. Values are validated when saved and again when read, because the LINE link becomes an `href` on every page. Keep `/` and `/quiz` static: the root layout's `revalidate` and the cache tag are what update them. Any server action that changes data must call `hasAdminAccess` itself.
- **Security fixes (penetration test PT-02 to PT-14, except PT-01 and PT-10):** keep the limits above working together: code requests are limited atomically, the backoffice login and the settings password are limited separately, and every limit and alert has a test in the penetration test scripts. Text that reaches the browser (`lib/otpErrors.ts`, anything a client component imports) must not name environment variables, because it ends up in a public script. Emails take the site address from `SITE_URL` or Netlify's `URL`, never from the Host header (development excepted). `OTP_SECRET` (optional) keys the code hashes; without it the admin password is used, and changing either cancels waiting codes. PT-10 (nonce-based content security policy) is not done on purpose: a nonce needs every page rendered per request, which would end the static `/` and `/quiz`; keep `'unsafe-inline'` until that trade-off is revisited. PT-01 (Next 16) is still open
- **Confirming changes:** with `TWO_FACTOR_AUTHEN` off, every settings change asks for the administrator password again (checked on the server against `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, with a 1 second pause on a wrong one, and a lock: after `PASSWORD_MAX_ATTEMPTS` wrong tries in a row (default 5, one count shared by everyone, kept in the `password_failures` table and added before the password is compared so a burst of parallel guesses cannot beat it) saving is refused for `PASSWORD_LOCK_MINUTES` (default 15), even with the right password, and the administrator is emailed once; a correct password starts the count again). With `TWO_FACTOR_AUTHEN=on` the password box is gone and a one-time password emailed to `ADMIN_EMAIL` approves the change instead; if a code can't be sent, saving is refused (fail closed) and never falls back to the password. The switch, `ADMIN_EMAIL` and the limits live only in the environment and must never become editable in the app, or someone with the backoffice password could switch it off or redirect the codes and warnings. The server reads `TWO_FACTOR_AUTHEN` on every save, never from a cached page or from the form. Never log the code or show it outside development, and never put the password or full long text in an email; the code email is the only one that carries a code.

## Deployment

Production is live at https://strategic-relationship.netlify.app/ on Netlify's free plan. Netlify's production branch is `release`, not `main`: pushing to `main` (where work and documents go) never deploys; the site deploys only when `release` moves (`git push origin main:release`, which publishes everything on `main`, or push a chosen commit to `release`). Never push to `release` unless the owner asks for a deploy. If Netlify's setting is changed back to `main`, every push to `main` deploys again. The database is Neon project `relationship-audit` (`lingering-band-55049917`, Siripod organization, Singapore, PostgreSQL 18.6).

- `netlify.toml` runs `db:migrate` on production builds only.
- `DATABASE_URL` must be Neon's pooled string. The pool in `lib/db.ts` is small and needs its `error` listener, because Neon suspends after 5 minutes and drops idle connections.
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD` lives in Netlify's dashboard, with a Production value and a scope that includes Functions. Variable changes need a new deploy. A missing value returns 503; a wrong one returns 401.
- Editing settings in production needs only `ADMIN_PASSWORD`. The change notification also needs `ADMIN_EMAIL` (recipient), `RESEND_API_KEY` and `EMAIL_FROM` (Production values, scope including Functions, then a new deploy); without them saving still works and the settings page says no email was sent. Test sending locally with `RESEND_API_URL=http://localhost:<port>/emails` pointing at a small server that records the request. Optional Netlify variables added by the security fixes (all need a new deploy): `SITE_URL` (site address in emails), `OTP_SECRET` (separate key for code hashes), `LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `LOGIN_LOCK_MINUTES`, `QUIZ_IP_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, `RESPONSES_PER_MINUTE`; `db:migrate` creates `login_failures`. Two-factor authentication is `TWO_FACTOR_AUTHEN=on` in Netlify (Production value, scope including Functions, then a new deploy); it needs the three email variables. If email stops working while it is on, nobody can save: fix the email variables, or remove `TWO_FACTOR_AUTHEN`, and deploy. `db:migrate` creates the `settings` table and seeds the course rows on deploy; it compiles `lib/courses.ts` with `typescript`, so that must stay installed at build time.
- Maintenance mode is the only off switch, because Netlify has no server process to stop: add `MAINTENANCE_MODE=on` in Netlify (Production value, scope including Functions) and deploy; remove it and deploy to reopen. Each change is a deploy (15 credits). Keep the page free of scripts and external files so it can't fail with the rest of the site.
- Every deploy (a push to `release`, or Trigger deploy in the dashboard) uses 15 of the free plan's 300 credits, so group changes. Before deploying, check that the newest commit being pushed to `release` does not contain `[skip netlify]`, which would make Netlify skip it. Check the Deploys page for the commit that is live; `git log release -1` should match it.

**Treat any `.env` created by `neon init` as production.** It points `DATABASE_URL` at the live database, so running the app locally against it reads and writes real responses. Check where it points before testing, and use a local database (`npm run db:dev`) instead.

To check the live site without saving data, use an invalid POST to `/api/responses` (expect 400) and an unknown UUID at `/results/` (404 proves the database connection works). Finishing the quiz saves a real row.

**Exception: `docs/Installation Manual.docx` is now the source of the installation manual.** The owner edited that Word file by hand (from 2026-11-11 its title is "Installation Manual: Ajkwan Relationship Assessment"), so keep it as it is: never re-export the online installation manual over it, and make any change to this manual by editing the Word file itself (python-docx or the owner). The online installation manual is no longer kept up to date. For every other document, the rule below still holds.

The online documents are the source: [design specification](https://claude.ai/artifact/G2J9Ecv4tkGDhbzJv2EYxy) and [installation manual](https://claude.ai/artifact/Eq2Vq1PZrMiUnGU2JnaR4P). A fourth online document, the [security review report](https://claude.ai/artifact/EiXGtGoW1XveLd4YxavXpV) (findings, fixes and how to repeat the checks; online only, no Word copy), complements them. A third online document, the [system administration manual](https://claude.ai/artifact/6qbfJSy1HYnsffFVMErc7B), covers running Netlify, Neon and the backoffice settings (shutdown and startup, maintenance mode, routine tasks); its Netlify screenshots were taken from the signed-in console with secrets hidden, and Neon has none yet. Update the online documents first, then refresh the Word copies in `docs/` (all three have one; the exporter leaves the results-page screenshot of the administration manual as a text placeholder, so after each re-export put `08-results-courses` back by adding it to `word/media`, a relationship in `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` and a drawing paragraph copied from another image, then check the file opens). The exports are large enough (they contain drawings or screenshots) to be saved to a file by the tool, which can be decoded exactly; never retype an inline base64 export, because that corrupted a file twice. The installation manual covers Netlify and Neon only, and its drawings are redrawn menu paths, not screenshots. Ignore Word's `~$` lock files in `docs/`.

**Word layout (owner's rule):** every Word file in `docs/` has exactly one table of contents with page numbers, and the numbers must match the headings. It is a Word TOC field (headings level 2 to 3), on its own page right after the title and date; the body starts on the next page. Every page has a header with the document name and a footer with "Page X / Y". Do this after each export or edit, and check it: open the file with Word (COM), update the fields, and compare each heading's real page with its TOC entry, then save. The hand-written "Contents" list in the online documents (links to headings) is only for reading online: remove it from the exported HTML before building the Word file, or the file gets two tables of contents. The online editor has no page header, footer, page numbers or automatic contents.

## Pitfalls

- Dev builds to `.next-dev` and production to `.next`. `next dev` crashes in the browser with `__webpack_require__.n is not a function` if it reuses production output, so keep them separate.
- `.glass-card` uses `backdrop-filter`, which traps `position: fixed` children. Render popups into `document.body` with a portal.
- `npm run db:dev` fails with "Postgres init script exited with code 1" in deeply nested Windows folders, because of the 260-character path limit. Use a short path such as `C:\dev\relationship-audit`.
- Node 18.17 is the minimum, and the reason Next.js stays on version 14. A `TRACE` request makes Next's middleware answer 500 under `next start` (it cannot build such a request); no detail leaks, and the host platform answers TRACE first.
- Backoffice login lock: anyone can call `/api/auth/check` or send wrong logins, so a guesser can lock the administrator out of the backoffice for `LOGIN_LOCK_MINUTES`. That is the cost of refusing the right password too during a lock. Recover by waiting, or delete the row (`DELETE FROM login_failures`) in the Neon SQL editor. Next 15 needs Node 18.18 and Next 16 needs Node 20.
- Build-time font download: `next build` needs internet access for Google Fonts.
- The Neon and Netlify CLIs need a newer Node than 18.17 (Neon needs 20.19 or newer). Use a temporary Node 22 if the machine is still on 18.
- Testing a server action in a browser: don't open the page as `http://admin:password@localhost:3000/...`. The action's request then fails with "Request cannot be constructed from a URL that includes credentials". Open that URL once to cache the login, then open the plain URL.
- Editing the database directly bypasses revalidation, so the prebuilt home page can keep an older LINE link for up to 5 minutes. Change settings through the app, or assert on the stored value in tests.
- `next.config.mjs` sends a strict Content-Security-Policy (own address only), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a Permissions-Policy on every response, switches off the image optimizer and removes `X-Powered-By`. If you add an external script, font, image host or embed (for example a QR service or analytics), add its address to the policy or the browser silently blocks it. Test on a production build, because development allows extra sources.
- A running `next dev` can keep using its old database after `.env` changes. Restart it, and confirm which database a test actually reached.
- The database must be UTF8 to store Thai text in `settings`. Neon is. `npm run db:dev` now creates new local clusters as UTF8, but a `.pgdata` made earlier on Windows is WIN1252 and fails with "has no equivalent in encoding WIN1252" when saving a course. Recreate the database as UTF8 (copy `responses` across) or delete `.pgdata`.
- Course forms must not be submittable before the page has loaded: a plain browser submit would be a GET that puts the password and text in the address bar. `CourseForm` keeps its buttons disabled until then.
- `answers` links to questions by position within the question set version stored with the response. Never read `answers` without that version, never count answers across versions, and never reorder the questions (the questions are fixed for this reason).
